title: A machine for writing the binary length
statement: There exist a natural number $K$, a finite state set $S$ with decidable equality, a deterministic machine $R$ with $K+1$ work tapes and Boolean symbols, entry and exit states in $S$, and a natural number $B$, such that for every Boolean word $x$ there is a time $t$ when $R$, started with the empty word on its first work tape and $x$ as input, is in the exit configuration with the binary expansion of $|x|$ on that tape. It has not reached the exit state at any earlier time $u<t$, and its total space use through time $t$ is at most $B$ times one plus the length of the binary expansion of $|x|$.
hypotheses_covered: $S$ is finite and has decidable equality
$R$ is a machine with $K+1$ work tapes and Boolean symbols
Entry and exit states belong to $S$
For every Boolean word $x$, there exists $t\in\mathbb N$
The run from the specified initial buffer configuration equals the exit configuration with $|x|$ in binary
No earlier time $u<t$ has state equal to the exit state
